blocks: Who speaks for shipping?
Industry presence in the delegations to the harbour conference
Eastmere Policy Lab, briefing paper
This briefing counts the delegates registered at the harbour conference whose organisations are tied to the shipping-fuel industry. It covers the conference's public register of participants.
Data and method

We used the conference's register of participants, 1,930 delegates in 61 delegations. Each delegate's organisation was looked up in the national company register to see whether it holds a licence to sell marine fuel.
Where the register gave no entry, the organisation's own website was used, and the case was marked as lower confidence.
Findings
We count 412 of 1,930 delegates as industry-linked, or 21 per cent.
Industry-linked delegates were concentrated in nine delegations, which together account for 300 of the 412.
Background
Port policy has been negotiated in this forum since its first session. Earlier briefings by other groups covered only the host country's delegation.
Shipping fuel accounts for a growing share of port emissions.
Limitations
Registration is not attendance: a registered delegate may never have come to the conference.
One person coded every organisation, so no measure of agreement between coders is available.
Governments should publish the employer of every delegate.
Annex: definitions
An industry-linked delegate is a delegate whose registered organisation holds a marine fuel sales licence, or is an association at least half of whose members hold one.
Delegates from government ministries are never counted as industry-linked, whatever their portfolio.
